verses.text: Then Elihu continued:
"Listen to my words, you wise men. Pay attention to me, you who know so much.
The ear tests words, just as the tongue tastes food.
Let's decide for ourselves what is right. Let's learn together what is good.
Job says, 'I am innocent, but God has refused me justice.
Even though I am right, I am called a liar. I have a wound that will not heal, even though I have done nothing wrong.'
Is there anyone like Job? He drinks up insults like water.
He keeps company with people who do evil. He spends time with wicked people.
He says, 'It does a person no good to try to please God.'
So listen to me, you men who understand. God would never do evil. The Almighty would never do wrong.
He pays people back for what they do. He gives them what their ways deserve.
It is true that God will never do wrong. The Almighty will never twist justice.
Did someone put him in charge of the earth? Did someone make him ruler of the whole world?
If he decided to take back his spirit and his breath,
every living thing would die together, and people would go back to the dust.
If you understand, listen to this. Pay attention to what I say.
Can someone who hates justice rule? Will you condemn the one who is fair and mighty?
He is the one who says to kings, 'You are worthless,' and to important people, 'You are wicked.'
He does not favor rulers or treat the rich better than the poor, because he made them all with his own hands.
People die suddenly in the middle of the night. They are shaken and pass away. The powerful are removed without human help.
God watches how people live. He sees every step they take.
There is no darkness or deep shadow where evil people can hide.
God does not need to look at a person very long before bringing him to judgment.
He breaks the powerful without needing to ask questions, and puts others in their place.
He knows what they do. He overthrows them in the night, and they are crushed.
He punishes them for their evil where everyone can see,
because they turned away from following him and paid no attention to any of his ways.
They made the poor cry out to God, and he heard the cry of those in need.
But if God stays quiet, who can blame him? If he hides his face, who can see him? Still, he watches over both nations and people,
so that godless people will not rule and trap the people.
Suppose someone says to God, 'I am guilty, but I will not sin any more.
Teach me what I cannot see. If I have done wrong, I will not do it again.'
Should God reward you on your terms, when you refuse to change? You must decide, not I. So tell me what you know.
People with understanding will agree with me, and every wise person who hears me will say,
'Job speaks without knowing what he is talking about. His words make no sense.'
I wish Job would be tested to the limit, because he answers like an evil man.
He adds rebellion to his sin. He claps his hands at us to mock us and keeps talking against God."
